title: This Calisthenics Freak Makes Bodybuilders Look Small (Baki_HD)
summary: Lifter profile of Baki, a French two-time street lifting world champion, reviewing three training days, his 'cultivate strength' philosophy and his physique. NH praises his low-volume, high-intensity, strict-technique approach, argues calisthenics upper body plus free-weight lower body is ideal for performance-based hypertrophy, and grades him the best physique he has ever rated.
claims: Baki, 27, won the street lifting world championship in 2021 and 2022 and placed second in 2023, losing only on the squat
Street lifting competitions judge four lifts: muscle-up, weighted pull-up, weighted dip and barbell back squat
Powerlifting is about 70-80% lower-body volume (squat, deadlift as hinge) and produces bottom-heavy, non-aesthetic physiques
Calisthenics/street workout is the king of performance sports for aesthetics and hypertrophy; when many athletes in a sport look great, something in their training should be copied
Pull-ups are an amazing hypertrophy movement, not a bad one, when done properly; they largely explain Baki's back
Baki's back day: controlled paused pull-up warm-ups, one top set of 2 at +80 kg, two backoffs of 3 at +60 kg, then 3x10 supinated rows at 100 kg, then ab wheel 3x10
Warm-up reps and top-set reps should have identical technique; never alter form to lift more
Do the bare effective minimum volume; junk volume only fatigues you and wastes time
Effort is a skill; strength athletes push to their maximum while many aesthetics trainees are big babies who never learn to push
Strength athletes increasingly isolate abs (e.g. Sam of Sheiko Gold/powerlifting channel), and bodybuilders should too
Do not copy the absence of arm isolation; pull-ups and rows alone are not enough stimulus for biceps and forearms for most people
A back day with one horizontal and one vertical pull is as effective as it gets if you like bro splits, though he dislikes that split
On dips, squeeze the triceps/elbows tight at the start, control a slow negative and explode up; losing the groove costs about 30% of performance
Dipping until the humerus is parallel to the floor is a legitimate full range of motion; going deeper is optional for bodybuilders
Baki's push/legs day: dips 1x2 at +120 kg, low-bar squat 1x6 with four plates, bench 3x5 at 120 kg with tempo
His high-bar to low-bar squat difference is about 20%
Use more than one horizontal press (bench, dumbbells, dips, ring or weighted push-ups) to reduce overuse injury risk and build carryover
Tempo bench 3x5 is close to hypertrophy work; a bodybuilder might do 3 sets of 5-10 instead
When pain limits an exercise, adapt by switching to a movement that does not hurt instead of pushing through or quitting
Mediocre powerlifters who use their own physiques as proof isolation is unnecessary are actually proof that it is necessary
Ideal program: train presses like Baki and complement with isolation work
Rarely testing 1RMs builds strength and physique better than constantly maxing, which tests strength rather than building it
Weighted Cossack squats train groin health, mobility and multi-directional joint patterns often ignored
Train joints in all the directions they can move so you do not tear your quads slipping on ice
Split squats beat shrimp and pistol squats for building mass
The perfect performance-based hypertrophy program is calisthenics for the upper body and free weights for the lower body; NH trains this way
Hip hinges like Zercher good mornings build the erectors that complete a back; lats alone are not impressive
Baki's competition bests: dip +170 kg, pull-up +107 kg, squat 250 kg, total 560 kg; Xavier Aubard holds the record 570 kg total via a 275 kg squat
Elite weighted dip at 200+ lb bodyweight is about +280 lb; Baki dips about three times what NH does
Because the squat moves the most weight, it dominates the street lifting total and advantages squat specialists, like the deadlift in powerlifting; the federation should rebalance
Strength is strength: Baki benched four plates after six weeks of bench specialisation thanks to his dip strength
Multiple pressing styles progress together; for bodybuilding it is ideal if they all rise slowly at once
Handstand push-ups get much harder as bodyweight rises; NH did them easily at 160 lb but cannot at 220 lb
A true hybrid athlete is excellent at many things, not mediocre at running and squatting
Baki has a strict curl of 70 kg and reps about 250 kg deadlift with hook grip without training it
Watching Dragon Ball or Baki growing up drives many of the biggest naturals; Baki started by hiking 30 min with a weighted backpack to a calisthenics park and training for hours
Calisthenics/street workout builds both an aesthetic body and spiritual strength, the 'cultivate strength' philosophy of a crusade against weakness
Genetics you cannot control, but being a genius of hard work is a learned skill
Baki is about 100 kg at maybe 12% body fat versus NH's 100 kg at 17-18%, a massive lean mass difference
He believes Baki is natural given steady progression and no signs of drugs; obsessing over natty status wastes training time
Baki got 3D delts with no lateral raises or overhead pressing, only dips and bench
Bodybuilders dismiss calisthenics movements because they are bad at them; NH ditched bench press for dips
Neck should be in line with the jaw as an aesthetic guideline
Grades: biceps S, triceps A (lacks long head), forearms B, shoulders S, chest S/A, upper back S, quads S, hamstrings A, glutes A, neck A, abs S: the best physique he has graded
The true genetic freaks go into lucrative sports; if they switched, they would wash out top powerlifters within two years
'Strength copers' who chose strength training because they could not build a physique lie to themselves
exercises: controlled negative, pause at top, same form on warm-ups and top set
crisp controlled negatives, posterior chain still, upper body does the work
squeeze triceps together, slow negative, explode up, humerus parallel to floor
groin health, mobility, multi-directional joint work
mass and unilateral work, better than pistols/shrimp squats
kettlebell held by teeth on a rope
vertical pressing strength; harder when heavy
stats: +135 lb x5 after ~1 year of dips (early intermediate)
training_log: added weight; about a year of dip training
